Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Load-In Schedule — The Lyric for one-nighter, touring band, house crew of eight
Resource limits: one loading dock, one stage, one lighting desk, one PA, one monitor world, one green room.
Everything must be finished by doors.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Load-In Schedule — The Lyric, one-nighter

One loading dock, one stage, one lighting desk, one PA, one monitor world. Crew call is 8am and that is where this schedule starts. The dock takes one truck at a time, so the lighting truck empties before the backline truck pulls in, and nothing goes up on stage while the dock is still moving through it.

Dock
Lighting truck in: bars, fixtures, cable, 60 minutes.
Backline truck in the moment the lighting truck is empty: 45 minutes.
Clear the dock and get the empties out; 15 minutes.

Lighting
Rig the bars as soon as the lighting truck is off the dock: 45 minutes on stage.
Focus from the desk once the rig is up: 60 minutes.
Build the cues after focus: 30 minutes if the plot is clean, up to 90 if it is not.
Strike the rig when the show is down: 60 minutes.

PA
Fly the PA as soon as the lighting truck is off the dock: 75 minutes.
Ring out the house: 20 minutes.

Monitors
Set monitor world once the backline truck is off the dock: 45 minutes.
Ring out the wedges: 20 minutes.

Band
Backline up as soon as the dock is clear of the second truck: 45 minutes on stage.
Soundcheck when the house and the wedges are both rung out: 60 minutes, drums first.
Band dinner after soundcheck: 60 minutes in the green room.

House
Set front of house from two hours in: 60 minutes, merch, bars, ushers.
Clean the house after the band go to dinner; 30 minutes.
Doors when the house manager calls them; 30 minutes of walk-up.
Show on stage once the house is in, and it runs as long as it runs.
Backline out fifteen minutes after the show is down: 45 minutes on the dock.

Notes
The dock is the first bottleneck and the stage is the second. Focus and cue-build both want the desk, so they are strictly sequential. Soundcheck is the only step in the day that waits on two separate departments at once.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This read-back is for a Rhylthyme run-of-show for a touring band’s one-night show at The Lyric, starting at the 8am crew call and organized around an eight-person house crew plus the band. The goal is to sequence dock unloading, lighting, PA, monitor world, band setup, front-of-house, soundcheck, band dinner, doors, and post-show load-out so the operation is ready by doors; however, the source gives no exact door time or date, and it also includes doors/show/strike steps that fall after the “finished by doors” constraint, so the true completion deadline cannot be anchored to a timestamp without inventing information. The provided text does not appear truncated, but it leaves the door time and the scope of “everything must be finished by doors” ambiguous.

```json
{
  "summary": "The run-of-show is for a touring band’s one-night show at The Lyric, beginning with an 8am crew call and coordinated for an eight-person house crew plus the band. It sequences dock deliveries, stage and rigging work, PA and monitor world setup, front-of-house preparation, soundcheck, band dinner, doors, and post-show load-out, with the stated aim that everything be finished by doors; the source does not provide an exact door time or date, and it also describes show and strike steps that occur after doors, so the deadline cannot be fixed without making up information. The main constraints are single shared resources — loading dock, stage, lighting desk, PA, monitor world, and green room — plus strict one-truck-at-a-time dock sequencing, sequential use of the lighting desk for focus and cue-build, soundcheck waiting on both house ringout and monitor wedge ringout, band dinner in the green room after soundcheck, and backline load-out delayed 15 minutes after the show is down.",
  "servesOrScale": "house crew of eight",
  "deadline": null,
  "constraints": [
    "one loading dock",
    "one stage",
    "one lighting desk",
    "one PA",
    "one monitor world",
    "one green room",
    "house crew of eight",
    "crew call starts the schedule at 08:00",
    "loading dock handles one truck at a time",
    "nothing goes up on stage while the dock is still moving through it",
    "lighting truck must empty before backline truck pulls in",
    "rigging starts only after the lighting truck is off the dock",
    "focus and cue-build must be sequential because they share the lighting desk",
    "PA flying starts only after the lighting truck is off the dock",
    "monitor world setup starts only after the backline truck is off the dock",
    "band backline up starts only after the dock is clear of the second truck",
    "soundcheck waits for both house ringout and monitor wedge ringout",
    "band dinner occurs after soundcheck and is in the green room",
    "front of house sets two hours into the schedule",
    "house cleaning occurs after the band goes to dinner",
    "doors are called by the house manager, with no exact time given",
    "show occurs once the house is in, with unspecified run length",
    "backline out begins 15 minutes after the show is down",
    "exact door deadline is not specified in the source"
  ]

```

A track is one ordered line of work, so any two activities that can happen at the same time belong on separate tracks rather than being chained inside one non-overlapping track. Each step has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with seconds, `variable` with min/max/default seconds, or `indefinite` until the person ends it. A step’s start trigger places it on the clock or behind another step using `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. `stepId`s are global across the whole program, so an `afterStep` reference must resolve to one uniquely named step and must not form a cycle. Every occupied `task` needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry’s `maxConcurrent` is the actual shared capacity that prevents two steps from using the same single resource at the same time. Repeated work is modeled as one step with `replicates`, then chained with `instances: "each"`, barriered with `instances: "all"`, and limited with `maxInFlight` when only k instances can be in flight at once.

Expected resource constraints from this run-of-show:

- `dock`: maxConcurrent 1 — one loading dock; eight crew may work it, but only one truck/load movement can occupy it.
- `stage`: maxConcurrent 1 — one stage; rigging, backline setup, soundcheck, show, and strike are stage-occupying work.
- `lighting_desk`: maxConcurrent 1 — one lighting desk/console; focus and cue-build must be sequential.
- `pa`: maxConcurrent 1 — one PA system/operator for flying the PA and ringing out the house.
- `monitor_world`: maxConcurrent 1 — one monitor world for monitor setup and wedge ringout.
- `green_room`: maxConcurrent 1 — one green room for band dinner.
- People working: eight explicit house crew; the touring band’s own headcount is not specified in the source.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "dock", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "stage", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "lighting_desk", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "pa", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "monitor_world", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "green_room", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 8
}
```

Turn 3 of 4 — extraction. Steps only: no tracks, no triggers, no program JSON.

Imagine you have to carry out this run-of-show yourself, in a venue where you have: one loading dock, one stage, one lighting desk, one PA, one monitor world, one green room, and everything must be ready at doors. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json

  "steps": [
    {
      "stepId": "roast-turkey",
      "name": "Roast the turkey",
      "task": "oven",
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or plan_event), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="doors" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
